title: Rabbah bar Tachlifa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Chullin 45b: “Rabbah bar Tachlifa said that Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba said that Rav said”; and in Shabbat 120a he spoke in Rav’s name. Therefore the She’erit Yosef listed him among Rav’s students. Hyman criticizes Seder HaDorot for writing that the reading should be that he spoke in Rava’s name; he did not look inside, as in Chullin 45b, where Abaye said to Rabbi Zeira: “What is your question? Did we not learn…, and Rabbah bar Tachlifa said…,” etc. Hyman argues that Abaye brings a proof for his words from Rabbah bar Tachlifa; how then can we say that he spoke in Rava’s name?

And what we find in Eruvin 40a, that Rava bar Tachlifa raised a difficulty against Ravina — they came before Rava — Hyman has already proposed that it was written רב״א, an abbreviation for Rav Acha bar Tachlifa, as explained in his entry.

notes.text: The Rav/Rava and proposed Rav Acha bar Tachlifa readings remain Hyman’s reasoning, not automatic harmonization. His argument from Abaye’s use of the teaching retains its rhetorical question.

The consulted Chullin 45b directly has Abaye addressing Zeira and citing Rabbah bar Tachlifa, Yirmeyah bar Abba and Rav. Hyman’s argument against the Rava reading, his She’erit Yosef report and proposed Rav Acha abbreviation in Eruvin remain separate attributed claims.
